newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't seeks to head off oil leaks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't seeks to head off oil leaks.

text.p: Argentina's government Monday signed a pact with five provinces to ensure proper monitoring of oil firms after recent damage to ducts caused leaks of crude into the Colorado River in central Argentina.

Environment Secretary Maria Julia Alsogaray signed the "Declaration of Neuquen" with envoys from Neuquen, La Pampa, Mendoza, Rio Negro and Buenos Aires, the five provinces the Colorado crosses on its way from the Andes to the Atlantic.

The companies YPF, Perez Companc, Petrolera San Jorge, Mexpetrol and Oldeval said in ads published in local newspapers earlier this week that the leaks were caused by torrential rains and slides of water and rocks "which are completely abnormal in the area."
As many as 300,000 liters of crude oil may have seeped into the river upstream, where the oil wells are located, after recent storms, according to media reports.

The firms claimed that before the latest leakages February 16 and March 6 they had hired international consultants to carry out an impact study but nobody had warned them of the risk of the present damage.

"There are no possible precautions you can take when 100 milimeters of rain fall in 20 minutes and a torrent of water digs up earth 3.5 meters (11.6 feet) deep, exposing pipes which are hit by rocks weighing up to two tonnes," they said.

Local authorities said the river had already cleansed itself to a large extent thanks to its strong current. But at least one province, Rio Negro, was considering suing the oil companies for damage to crops through lack of clean water.
